slides.title: Mechanism-guided redesign of the nylon hydrolase Nyl12
slides.subtitle: Quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) reaction pathways and transition-state-based enzyme design
slides.notes: Research progress briefing. Build date is rendered dynamically in America/New_York. The scientific evidence date is 25 November 2026. Nyl12 is a nylon-6 oligomer hydrolase; the current modeling target is a bounded redesign pilot, not an experimentally validated new enzyme. The cover image is a white-background molecular rendering from source-bound structures; hydrogen atoms are grey (#B8B8B8) and sticks use the validated 0.18 Å display setting.

slides.title: Transition-state models will guide Nyl12 redesign
slides.notes: The design objective is to create qualified transition-state (TS) templates from the WT mechanism, then use them to guide sequence design. LigandMPNN proposes sequences around constrained templates; Boltz-2 ranks structural compatibility; OpenMM evaluates matched molecular-dynamics behavior. TS means transition state. The engineering pipeline can be commissioned by 30 November, while nomination requires qualified WT templates and existing scientific gates.

slides.title: Nyl12 hydrolyzes PA6 with limited conversion
rows: 75 °C, 6 h; Tris pH 8. Active amount uncertain.
L4 modeled; L4 → two L2 is unproven.
slides.caption: PA6 = nylon-6. Assay systems differ; conversion is not kcat.
slides.notes: Published PA6 hydrolysis work reports linear oligomers, with trimers predominating; this preference is not attributed specifically to the crude-lysate assay. The crude lysate experiment used 75 °C for 6 h in 200 mM Tris pH 8; active enzyme amount and temperature-adjusted pH are uncertain. The purified-enzyme manuscript assay used 65 °C for 24 h in phosphate pH 7.4. Discordant K59E duplicate measurements are from crude lysate; they are not used as a clean activity label. L4 is an atomistic modeling hypothesis; formation of two L2 products is not experimentally established. No lysate conversion is treated as kcat.

slides.title: Mature Nyl12 exposes Thr233 as the β-chain N terminus
bullets: Mature enzyme: α chain 1–232 plus β chain 233–328.
Autocleavage exposes β-chain Thr233 as the N-terminal nucleophile.
Thr233 OG1 attacks; Phe113 and Asn186 stabilize oxyanion-like O.
slides.notes: The mature enzyme is an autocleaved N-terminal nucleophile hydrolase. The α chain comprises residues 1–232 and the β chain starts at Thr233 (residues 233–328). Autocleavage exposes Thr233 at the β-chain N terminus. The Thr233 side-chain hydroxyl initiates acylation; the newly exposed α-amino group is a candidate proton acceptor in a relay hypothesis. Phe113 and Asn186 form oxyanion-hole contacts in the modeled active site. Water-mediated deacylation regenerates the enzyme and releases the carboxyl product; the current pathway campaign focuses on acylation, and hydration/deacylation has not established complete hydrolysis.

slides.title: Acylation and deacylation complete the catalytic cycle
slides.takeaway: Acylation is in scope; water-mediated deacylation remains untested.

lanes.title: Cycle

slides.notes: E–S means enzyme–substrate complex. Acylation transfers the substrate acyl group to Thr233 and releases the amine-side product. The resulting acylenzyme is then attacked by water; deacylation releases the carboxylic-acid product (subsequent protonation depends on buffer conditions) and regenerates enzyme. Current QM/MM path work focuses on acylation. The hydration/deacylation follow-up has not yet supplied a qualified attacking-water model or a complete hydrolysis cycle.

slides.title: Substrate orientation sets the geometry for proton delivery
slides.caption: Two orientations: Nα–Nleave = 4.59 Å vs 3.62 Å; leaving-N proximity matters.
slides.notes: Nα denotes the Thr233 α-amino nitrogen; Nleave is the substrate scissile-amide nitrogen. With consistent scissile-amide atom mapping, signed Herschlag φ distinguishes the two local orientations. In these representative structures, negative φ is not the closer Nα–Nleave pose: 4.58775 Å versus 3.61882 Å for positive φ. Separate ensemble means are 4.65 versus 3.61 Å. Use the measured proton-donor/acceptor distances and hydrogen-bond geometry to assess delivery; do not use φ sign alone as a catalytic criterion. An initial substrate-bound structure is a model and may reorganize.

slides.title: A four-repeat PA6 oligomer defines the classical model scope

cards.title: End groups
cards.text: NH₃⁺ and COO⁻; internal amides are neutral.

cards.title: Not checked
cards.text: Other lengths, bulk polymer, reactive states.

slides.notes: The released RESP/GAFF2 parameterization is validated for zwitterionic L4 only. It does not certify a reactive intermediate or an arbitrary polymer length. The compact-conformer electrostatic holdout did not pass. Reactive pathway calculations use QM/MM rather than assuming the classical substrate force field is valid for TI1 or acylenzyme states. L4 is a four-repeat nylon-6 oligomer. The modular residue labels are P6N (+1), P6I (neutral), P6I (neutral), P6C (−1); these internal labels are kept in notes rather than presented as chemical names.

slides.title: PA6 L4 bonded profiles pass all eight force-field checks
slides.caption: Two representative profiles; all eight declared bonded-profile gates passed.
slides.notes: The current PA6 L4 release passes all eight declared bonded-profile gates. The parameterization combines RESP charges, GAFF2 substrate terms, ff19SB protein and TIP3P water. The compact-conformer electrostatic holdout failed, so the release is scoped to the validated zwitterionic L4 model and bonded validation; it is not a blanket validation of all PA6 electrostatics or reactive states.

slides.title: Three 500 ps molecular-dynamics replicas support the L4 model
slides.caption: Three 500 ps validation replicas; stability supports the stated L4 use only.
slides.notes: The parameter release passed three 500 ps validation replicas for zwitterionic L4. These are force-field validation simulations, separate from WT enzyme protonation-state MD. Stability does not validate a reactive TI1/acyl state, arbitrary chain length, or nylon material behavior. The compact electrostatic holdout failure remains a documented limitation.

slides.title: The NylC catalytic-triad proposal motivated Asp protonation tests

cards.title: Interpretation
cards.text: Motivates testing; assigns no pKa population.

slides.notes: Negoro et al. (2023) motivates evaluating the Asp pair, but the reported NylC mechanistic proposal does not assign a protonation state to mature Nyl12. Mapping is Asp306→Asp272, Asp308→Asp274, Thr267→Thr233. Precursor structures vary in mutations and cleavage state, confounding maturation comparisons. The mature Nyl12 active-site environment is not identical to the NylC precursor site. The early Nyl12 ASH272 hypothesis followed the NylC Asp306 proposal. Exploratory QM/MM optimizations transferred that proton to Asp274, motivating a matched ASH274 WT MD follow-up. This is an observed model relaxation, not a pKa population assignment or proof that Nyl12 Asp274 is protonated.
slides.takeaway: Negoro et al., FEBS J. 2023; doi:10.1111/febs.16755

cards.text: Structure and ligand state change estimates.

cards.title: MCCE
cards.text: Quality checks incomplete; values not interpreted.

slides.notes: ASP denotes deprotonated carboxylate COO−; ASH denotes protonated carboxylic acid COOH. The Thr233 N-terminal amine can be neutral NH2 or protonated NH3+. These states are explicit hypotheses for matched simulation, not automatic assignments. PROPKA estimates are sensitive to starting conformation, ligand state and coupling. MCCE quality checks are incomplete; values are not interpreted as microscopic pKa results. In mature NylC structures, the nearest Asp oxygen separation is about 3.91 Å, not evidence for a short shared-proton bond. NylC values must not be presented as Nyl12 pKa values. The pKa and protonation terminology is defined here before the matched MD protocol.

slides.title: Matched wild-type (WT) simulations compare three protonation states
slides.caption: Fixed-charge simulations near 300 K; states test conditional structure, not protonation populations.
slides.notes: WT means wild type. All three sets used four independent 100 ns replicas with matched preparation and analysis near 300 K. Each row names the N-terminal amino state and Asp272/Asp274 carboxyl state. Fixed-charge trajectories estimate conditional structural occupancy within the specified state; they do not measure pKa or equilibrium populations between states. Earlier unmatched ASH272 trajectories are not pooled.

slides.title: Attack geometry and oxyanion contacts define the structural screen
slides.caption: φ is a signed local peptide-orientation metric, not evidence of proton transfer.
slides.notes: The strict and broad sets replace unexplained Tier A/B labels. Distances are Thr233 OG1 to scissile C, Phe113 backbone N to carbonyl O, and Asn186 ND2 to carbonyl O. The Bürgi–Dunitz angle describes nucleophile approach; signed Herschlag φ reports local amide orientation, and |φ| is used in these geometry bins. A separate Nα–Nleave distance evaluates possible proton delivery. Geometry occupancy is not catalytic activity or a protonation-state measurement. The native-Thr diagnostic is retained as a diagnostic because known-active controls expose false negatives.

slides.title: Asp274 protonation did not improve matched WT geometry occupancy
slides.caption: Bars are four-replica means; error bars show between-replica sample SD.
slides.notes: The plotted observable is the fraction of frames meeting either the stringent or broader defined attack/oxyanion-hole geometry set. Means ± between-replica SD: NH2/ASP272/ASP274 27.77 ± 24.64%; NH2/ASP272/ASH274 5.18 ± 6.80%; NH3+/ASP272/ASP274 28.99 ± 12.99%. Native-Thr occupancy is 0.0175%, 0.245%, and 0%, respectively. These are correlated structural observations from four replicas, not activity, rate, or protonation population. The ASH274 state did not improve occupancy under this matched protocol.

cards.text: Reactive center, scissile amide, polar contacts.

cards.title: QM/MM boundary
cards.text: Eight link H; selected substrate/protein cuts.

slides.notes: The current branch uses 98 real QM atoms, eight Amber link hydrogens, charge −2, and 4,165 mobile MM atoms in the 12 Å environment; atoms outside that region are frozen. No molecular image is used here; the active-site context render is not the exact QM subsystem. Native QM membership from model/inputs/dimer.mdin and system.prmtop: Ile112 partial segment (17 atoms, no backbone N); Phe113 partial segment (18 atoms, N/H/CA plus side chain, no C/O); Asn186 side chain (8); full Thr233 (15); partial Thr234 segment (12, no C/O); Asp272 and Asp274 side chains (6 each); and two local PA6 amide fragments (8 atoms each). There are no QM waters. This concise list does not imply the whole Phe113 or PA6 backbone is QM.

slides.title: Fixed-geometry QM benchmarks test distinct transformations
slides.caption: Reference: ωB97X-D/def2-SVP. Fixed-geometry comparisons; no barrier validation.
slides.notes: The coupled-path panel compares six fixed geometries with ωB97X-D/def2-SVP; DFTB3 relative-profile RMSE is 3.27 kcal/mol and error reaches +7.42 kcal/mol for the TI1-like structure. Point-charge membership varied across windows (8104–7999), so this is a finite-embedding method diagnostic, not a validated reaction-energy profile; a fixed-membership check remains. A separate five-window matched electrostatic-embedding benchmark tests Thr233 OH→Nα proton transfer (not direct transfer to substrate amide N): DFTB3 RMSE 1.49 kcal/mol, endpoint error −0.57; GFN2-xTB RMSE 3.91, endpoint +7.93. Neither fixed-geometry comparison establishes gradients, a stationary point, a barrier, or a PMF.

slides.title: MM and QM/MM minimization refine MD-derived E–S structures
slides.notes: The workflow begins from equilibrated enzyme–substrate (E–S) snapshots sampled under explicit protonation states. Validate atom mapping, proton inventory, covalent connectivity and QM/MM membership before minimization. MM minimization removes local strain in the chosen classical model. DFTB3/MM minimization then treats the reactive center quantum mechanically. These steps refine starting structures; they do not guarantee every snapshot is catalytically competent or prove a stable intermediate. Reactive TI1/acyl states are not accepted using the PA6 classical force field alone.

slides.title: Reaction-path optimization and free-energy sampling
slides.takeaway: PES: potential energy; PMF: sampled free energy.
slides.notes: Coordinate driving constructs a chemically guided starting path. Nudged elastic band (NEB) optimizes a chain of images on the potential-energy surface (PES); the maximum is a TS candidate, not automatically a verified saddle. Transition-state qualification requires curvature and downhill connectivity. Umbrella sampling runs biased molecular dynamics windows, then reweights the samples. WHAM (weighted histogram analysis method) and MBAR (multistate Bennett acceptance ratio) estimate the potential of mean force (PMF), a free-energy profile. WHAM (weighted histogram analysis method) cross-checking is planned, not completed. MBAR is the multistate Bennett acceptance ratio. These two outputs answer different questions and require separate acceptance.
slides.caption: NEB = nudged elastic band; WHAM = weighted histogram analysis method; MBAR = multistate Bennett acceptance ratio.

slides.title: Two proposed acylation mechanisms differ in proton transfer
slides.caption: A: Thr233 OH → amide N; B: OH → Nα → amide N. TI1: tetrahedral intermediate.
slides.notes: Mechanism A transfers the Thr233 side-chain hydroxyl proton directly to the scissile substrate amide nitrogen as Thr233 OG1 attacks the substrate carbonyl. Mechanism B relays that proton first to the Thr233 N-terminal α-amino group (Nα), then from Nα to the substrate amide nitrogen during acylation. These are distinct hypotheses. Similar E–S endpoints or product composition do not establish a shared frozen reference, Hamiltonian, sampling coordinate, or comparable free-energy profile.

slides.title: Direct proton transfer: DFTB3/MM NEB profile
slides.caption: Mechanism A potential-energy path; the highest band image is not a verified transition state.
slides.notes: This canonical band contains the direct Thr233 OG1–H to scissile substrate amide-N route (Mechanism A), with DFTB3/MM energies. The maximum is about 35.81 kcal/mol relative to the stated E–S reference. The band is converged as a NEB path, but the highest image has not been verified as an index-1 transition state with a downhill connection. Treat the plotted value as a potential-energy profile (PES) maximum, not ΔG‡. It is not directly comparable with the N-terminal-relay PES without common Hamiltonian/reference/coordinate analysis.

slides.title: Direct-seeded umbrella sampling reveals competing proton-transfer channels
slides.caption: q_acyl is the projected acylation coordinate; this mixed-channel marginal is unconverged.
slides.notes: The latest 22 November 2026 retained q_acyl marginal is about 47.05 kcal/mol for direct-seeded umbrella sampling. The 63-window dataset includes configurations with competing proton-transfer channels, including N-terminal-relay-like frames, so this is not a route-pure Mechanism A PMF. Target effective sample size was about 7.29, with drift flags in windows 028/030/032. It is preliminary and unconverged. Its q_acyl projection/reference differs from the three-coordinate arclength profile used for Mechanism B, so the maxima must not be directly subtracted.

slides.title: Bias-free optimization retained an addition-like structure
slides.caption: This optimization retained an addition-like, relay-ready structure.
slides.notes: The w033 internal candidate came from direct-seeded umbrella MD, which also sampled N-terminal-relay configurations; umbrella bias was then removed before QM/MM optimization. This lineage explains how an addition-like relay structure emerged from a direct-seeded campaign. It retained partial tetrahedral character with C–OG1=1.740 Å, C–N=1.490 Å, C–O=1.309 Å; gradient was 7.94×10⁻⁶ Eh/bohr. Label it addition-like or TI1-like, not a proven stable TI1 minimum. Full Hessian/minimum curvature and an unbiased lifetime are not established. This active-site rendering contains 152 local atoms and provides context only; it is not a visualization of the exact 98-real-atom QM subsystem. E–S/acyl endpoints may share chemical composition but not automatically a common frozen environment/reference.
slides.takeaway: Direct-seeded umbrella MD → bias-free QM/MM optimization.

slides.title: Proton-relay acylation: DFTB3/MM potential-energy profile
slides.caption: Relative potential energy along the coordinate-driven path; ΔEmax = 16.31 kcal/mol.
slides.notes: Joined DFTB3/MM coordinate-driven path, referenced to regenerated E–S under the current pathway Hamiltonian and frozen exterior. The physical energy excludes driving bias. The connected maximum is ΔE=16.312 kcal/mol; acyl endpoint is −4.15 kcal/mol. Endpoint optimization gradients were small, but the forward dimer candidate’s first-order curvature and downhill connectivity remain unverified; the reverse candidate search had SCC failures and is not used for TS qualification. This is a PES, not a PMF or verified TS barrier. Matching the E–S chemistry to Mechanism A does not prove the frozen coordinates, Hamiltonian, QM membership, or reference are identical. The B path was constructed in reverse toward E–S and forward toward acylenzyme from the addition-like candidate. Its zero is the separately released E–S endpoint, not automatically the zero of the original A ensemble.
slides.takeaway: PES maximum ΔE ≈ 16.31 kcal/mol from released E–S; ΔG‡ pending.

slides.title: Umbrella sampling tests the Mechanism B free-energy profile
slides.status: Production sampling in progress; PMF pending
slides.detail: 57 windows at 300 K; coverage, overlap and stability gates remain.
slides.notes: The current N-terminal-relay umbrella campaign has 57 windows at 300 K. Production is organized into short 5 ps blocks following heating/equilibration and workflow acceptance. Do not show a filled PMF curve or completion date while analysis is pending. WHAM and MBAR refer to histogram-based and multistate Bennett free-energy estimators; any estimator must pass the same coverage/overlap, block stability, hysteresis and chemical-retention gates. Sampling completion, convergence, and mechanism qualification are separate outcomes.

slides.title: Matched free-energy calculations will compare the two mechanisms
slides.status: Common physical model confirmed; matched-coordinate analysis pending
slides.message: Topology and QM/MM masks agree within restart precision.
slides.detail: Mechanism A uses q_acyl; B uses path/arclength. Shared-coordinate reanalysis remains pending.
slides.notes: A new compatibility audit confirmed exact topology hash 448560…, the same 98-real-atom QM mask and −2 charge, 4,165-atom mobile mask, 300 K MD / 0 K electronic setup, shared 16-file 3OB tree, and native Ewald/PME cutoffs. The 100,757 frozen atoms in A seeds 001/004/009/012/024 and the B seed agree to maximum XYZ difference 3.81×10⁻⁶ Å (RMS 1.56×10⁻⁶ Å; maximum per-atom displacement 6.32×10⁻⁶ Å); six cell parameters match exactly. A uses SCF energy tolerance 1×10⁻¹⁰ and B 1×10⁻¹², a numerical rather than chemical Hamiltonian difference. A stricter-tolerance/numerical-precision check remains before pooling. Even with a compatible physical model, the current profiles are not directly comparable: A is a branch-mixed, unconverged q_acyl marginal; B uses path arclength and has no PMF. Reanalyze retained A frames and B samples on a shared coordinate, E–S basin and normalization before interpreting barriers. The B coordinate path starts at its released E–S structure; identical chemical composition is not proof that this is the same conformational basin as the A q_acyl reference.

slides.title: Transition-state verification requires curvature and downhill connectivity
slides.message: No verified index-1 transition state or complete downhill connection is established.
slides.detail: Pending checks: stationary-point curvature, eigenvector direction, and connected descent to the intended chemical basins.
slides.notes: A high NEB image or PES maximum is not by itself a transition state. The current relay candidate needs first-order saddle curvature (one imaginary mode along the reaction coordinate) and downhill connectivity into the intended E–S and acyl basins. A stationary-point search can terminate computationally without meeting these scientific acceptance criteria. No full-Hessian result should be implied while verification is in progress.

slides.title: Transition-state templates guide symmetry-aware sequence design
slides.notes: Design templates should be derived from an ensemble of chemically checked WT transition-state-like structures, with key catalytic atoms and symmetry-related design positions defined before sequence sampling. LigandMPNN supplies sequence proposals under the protected-site mask. Boltz-2 evaluates structural compatibility. OpenMM uses matched protocols for WT/design comparison. An unverified candidate or ES-trained force field does not become a TS template. The existing geometry gates remain in force; do not relax them to meet a deadline.

slides.title: Appendix: Eyring rates illustrate barrier sensitivity to temperature
slides.takeaway: k = (k_B T/h) exp[−ΔG‡/(RT)], κ = 1; rates in s⁻¹.
slides.caption: An assumed ΔG‡ at each temperature; this is not a measured barrier or a polymer-conversion prediction.
slides.notes: Elementary Eyring rates assume transmission coefficient κ=1 and a specified activation free energy at each temperature. The calculation does not predict the temperature dependence of the barrier. Lysate conversion depends on active-enzyme concentration, substrate accessibility, adsorption, binding and product release. A potential-energy maximum cannot be inserted as ΔG‡.

slides.title: Appendix: PROPKA estimates depend on structure and cleavage state
slides.caption: Nyl12: Asp272/Asp274/Thr233; NylC: Asp306/Asp308/Thr267. Ranges span structures/chains.
slides.notes: These are default PROPKA estimates across retained structure/chain preparations; ranges are observed across structures/chains, not confidence intervals. Nyl12 primary site E includes three static geometries: Asp272 0.88–2.37, Asp274 3.44–6.95, Thr233 Nα 8.93–9.70. Mature NylC 5XYG default estimates are Asp306 2.19–2.21, Asp308 5.49–6.49, and Thr267 N 6.35–6.55. Uncleaved precursor structures 7YU0 and 7YU1 contain mutations; they were not back-mutated, so cleavage and mutation effects are confounded. The Thr N terminus is not free in these uncleaved structures. Coupled-state alternatives vary substantially and are not a unique assignment. MCCE quality checks are incomplete; its values are not interpreted. A ~3.91 Å nearest Asp O–O separation is discussed in the NylC mechanism notes, not mixed into this pKa table.

slides.title: Appendix: sources, coordinate definitions, and interpretation limits
bullets: PES: potential energy along a path; it is not a free-energy profile.
PMF: potential of mean force from sampled, bias-corrected configurations.
TS: transition state requires stationary-point curvature and downhill connectivity.
E–S: enzyme–substrate complex; acylenzyme: covalent enzyme–substrate intermediate.
WHAM/MBAR: histogram and multistate estimators; overlap and stability checks remain required.
All figures and scientific inputs are mapped with source hashes in asset_sources.json and the build receipt.
slides.notes: PES means potential-energy surface/profile and is distinct from a potential of mean force (PMF), which estimates a free-energy profile from sampled biased configurations. A transition-state assignment requires stationary-point curvature and downhill connections. E–S is enzyme–substrate; acylenzyme is the covalent intermediate after substrate acylation. WHAM is the weighted histogram analysis method and MBAR is the multistate Bennett acceptance ratio; neither rescues poor overlap or unstable sampling. Primary inputs, caveats, and per-slide references are retained in slide notes and the hashed receipt.
